chunks: Ibn Abi Nasr, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A man from Sistan came to him and said to him, 'We have dirhams called 'al-Shahiyyah' which are valued at two dananqs more than the standard dirham.' He said, 'There is no harm with it if it is permissible (circulating/accepted).'

key_terms.الشَّاهِيَّةُ: Al-Shahiyyah (a specific type of coin or currency)
key_terms.دَانِقَيْنِ: Two dananqs (a fractional unit of currency)
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: Permissible/Valid (in the context of circulation or acceptance)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using local currency with a value premium in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of recognizing local currency variations based on customary acceptance (*ijaz*) rather than rigid intrinsic value parity. It highlights the flexibility in commercial transactions (*mu'amalat*) where the Imam permits the 'Shahiyyah' coin despite its premium, provided it is legally valid and widely accepted in its region of origin.
